questions.text: Does the platform expose a public, documented API?

options.label: Yes, but docs are sparse, outdated, or partner-gated
No public API
options.gap: No public, documented API — the baseline requirement before any agent integration can start.

options.label: API key only, account-wide access
options.gap: Auth is API-key-only with no scoping, so an agent gets full account access with no way to limit blast radius.

options.label: Shared login, session cookies, or no formal auth
options.gap: No formal, scoped authentication model — an agent would have to impersonate a human session.

questions.text: Can API clients write data back to the platform, not just read?

options.label: Yes, full read/write across core objects
Limited write — a subset of objects only
options.gap: Write access is limited to a subset of objects, which caps what an agent can actually do end to end.

options.label: Read-only
options.gap: The API is read-only — an agent can observe but never take action.

questions.text: Are writes idempotent — safe to retry without side effects (idempotency keys, upsert semantics)?

options.label: Partially — only on some endpoints
options.gap: Idempotency is only partially documented, so a retried agent action can be unsafe on some endpoints.

options.label: No, or not documented
options.gap: Writes aren't documented as idempotent — a retried agent action can silently double-write or duplicate records.

questions.text: Are destructive writes reversible (soft delete, versioning, rollback)?

options.label: Partially
options.gap: Some destructive writes have no rollback path, so a subset of agent mistakes are unrecoverable.

options.label: No — deletes are permanent
options.gap: Destructive writes are permanent — one bad agent action has no undo.

questions.text: Is there an audit log for API-driven changes, queryable via the API?

options.label: Yes, full audit trail available via the API
Exists in the UI only, not API-accessible
options.gap: The audit trail is UI-only, so an agent operator has no programmatic way to review what an agent did.

options.label: No audit log
options.gap: No audit log for API-driven changes — agent actions are effectively untraceable.

questions.text: Does the platform support webhooks or an event stream for changes?

options.label: Yes, webhooks or an event stream
Polling only
options.gap: Change notification is polling-only, which wastes an agent's cycles and adds latency to reactions.

options.label: No
options.gap: No webhook or event stream — an agent can only find out about changes by polling blind.

questions.text: Are rate limits documented, with limits surfaced in response headers?

options.label: Yes, documented and returned in response headers
Documented but not in headers
options.gap: Rate limits are documented but not exposed in headers, so an agent can't self-throttle dynamically.

options.label: Not documented
options.gap: Rate limits are undocumented — an agent has no way to self-throttle and will get throttled or banned blind.

questions.text: Is there a sandbox/test environment and/or an MCP server or agent-specific integration docs?

options.label: Yes — both a sandbox and MCP/agent docs
One of the two
options.gap: Only one of sandbox or agent-specific docs exists, so agent builders are partly flying blind.

options.label: Neither
options.gap: No sandbox and no agent-specific integration path — every agent build starts by testing against production.
